{"id": "68484a0e-e53e-4a23-9fb0-fed3f47c5ef7", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Result: CIS 2.1.1 and PCI DSS 10.2.1 both fail. I couldn't confirm what AWS-1 checks, so I can't give it a status.**

This assessment uses only the logging config you gave me. I didn't touch the cluster.

| Check | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CIS Amazon EKS 2.1.1 (Enable audit logs) | **FAIL** | Audit logging is disabled. The `api` and `authenticator` log types don't satisfy this control. |
| PCI DSS v4.0.1 10.2.1 | **FAIL** | AWS Security Hub maps this requirement to control EKS.8, which fails when the `audit` log type isn't enabled. |
| Supplementary check AWS-1 | **Not determined** | I couldn't find a documented check with that ID in the AWS docs. |

- **CIS 2.1.1:** The EKS best-practices guidance treats audit logs as a separate part of the control plane logs. They hold the record of who did what through the Kubernetes API.
- **PCI DSS 10.2.1:** Requirement 10.2.1 covers audit logs that capture individual user access and administrative actions. Having `api` and `authenticator` logs on doesn't make up for missing `audit` logs.
- **AWS-1:** If you paste its definition, I'll evaluate it against your config. If it's an internal or tool-specific check, such as one from a scanner or a custom checklist, I'd need that definition to rate it. I'd rather not guess a status.

**Fix for both failures:** enable the `audit` log type in the cluster's control plane logging. It ships to CloudWatch Logs, which adds storage cost. Kubernetes audit entries can also be larger than the 1 MB CloudWatch Logs entry limit, so very large entries may be truncated to request metadata. I can make that change with your approval if you want me to.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
